### GTFS Rail Stops

Filter GTFS stops to Light Rail (TRAX, route_type 0) and Commuter Rail
(FrontRunner, route_type 2) only, walking the routes → trips → stop_times chain.

::: {#272faf31 .cell execution_count=7}
``` {.python .cell-code}
feed = gk.read_feed(PATHS["in_gtfs"], dist_units="km")

gdf_stops  = gk.get_stops(feed,  as_gdf=True).to_crs(PROJ_UTM12N)
gdf_shapes = gk.get_shapes(feed, as_gdf=True).to_crs(PROJ_UTM12N)
gdf_routes = gk.get_routes(feed, as_gdf=True).to_crs(PROJ_UTM12N)

RAIL_ROUTE_TYPES = {0, 2}   # 0 = Light Rail (TRAX/S-Line), 2 = Commuter Rail (FrontRunner)
RAIL_MODE_MAP = {0: "light_rail", 2: "commuter_rail"}

rail_route_ids = feed.routes.loc[feed.routes["route_type"].isin(RAIL_ROUTE_TYPES), "route_id"]
rail_trip_ids  = feed.trips.loc[feed.trips["route_id"].isin(rail_route_ids), "trip_id"]

# stop_id -> mode. Every rail stop_id is served by exactly one route_type in
# this feed (verified directly: 0 stops serve more than one), but two
# same-named stations (Murray Central, Salt Lake Central) DO share a
# stop_name across modes -- distinct physical platforms that happen to carry
# the same station name. That's why the D3 grouping below keys on
# (stop_name, mode), not stop_name alone.
rail_stop_times = feed.stop_times[feed.stop_times["trip_id"].isin(rail_trip_ids)].merge(
    feed.trips[["trip_id", "route_id"]], on="trip_id",
).merge(
    feed.routes[["route_id", "route_type"]], on="route_id",
)
stop_mode_lookup = (
    rail_stop_times.drop_duplicates("stop_id")
    .set_index("stop_id")["route_type"]
    .map(RAIL_MODE_MAP)
)

gdf_rail_stops = gdf_stops[gdf_stops["stop_id"].isin(stop_mode_lookup.index)].copy()
gdf_rail_stops["mode"] = gdf_rail_stops["stop_id"].map(stop_mode_lookup)
print(f"Rail stops: {len(gdf_rail_stops):,} of {len(gdf_stops):,} total stops")
print(gdf_rail_stops["mode"].value_counts().to_string())
```

### GTFS Rail Shapes

Physical track geometry, one canonical shape per route (not per `shape_id`).
A GTFS route typically publishes several `shape_id` variants — one per
direction plus express/short-turn patterns — that all retrace the *same*
physical track independently, each with its own slightly different GPS
digitization. Naively dissolving every variant together (`unary_union` +
`linemerge`, the same approach that works cleanly for `CandidateTDMRoadLinks`
in `02_create_link.qmd`) was tested directly against this feed and fails
badly here: GEOS nodes the output at every point where two near-duplicate
traces diverge by even a few centimetres, and — worse — a single shape can
be non-`simple` on its own (self-crossing GPS noise), which explodes it into
fragments all by itself. Confirmed directly: dissolving FrontRunner's 7 raw
shape variants together produced 297 chains (mean length 528 m) instead of
one clean ~130 km corridor; even its single longest shape alone is
non-simple and explodes into 5 pieces under `unary_union`.

Forward and backward service run the *same* physical track, so a single
direction's shape is a complete representation of a route's alignment —
there is no need to reconcile multiple variants at all. For each route, we
keep only its longest shape (the fullest end-to-end trace) and use it
as-is, self-intersections and all: `split_candidate_links` in
`02_create_link.qmd` cuts by M-value projection, which works correctly
on a non-simple line, so the self-crossing noise is harmless as long as we
never ask GEOS to topologically re-node it. Different routes that
genuinely share physical trackage (e.g. TRAX Blue/Red through downtown)
end up as separate, near-duplicate overlapping pieces after splitting —
by design, the same pattern already used everywhere else in this pipeline
for a two-way street digitized as two directional rows.

::: {#d4f9c63f .cell execution_count=9}
``` {.python .cell-code}
trip_shape_route = (
    feed.trips.loc[feed.trips["trip_id"].isin(rail_trip_ids), ["route_id", "shape_id"]]
    .dropna(subset=["shape_id"])
    .merge(feed.routes[["route_id", "route_type"]], on="route_id")
    .drop_duplicates("shape_id")
)
trip_shape_route["mode"] = trip_shape_route["route_type"].map(RAIL_MODE_MAP)

gdf_shapes_utm = gdf_shapes.to_crs(CRS_UTM)
gdf_shapes_utm["length_m"] = gdf_shapes_utm.geometry.length
shape_lengths = trip_shape_route.merge(gdf_shapes_utm[["shape_id", "length_m"]], on="shape_id")

canonical_idx = shape_lengths.groupby("route_id")["length_m"].idxmax()
gdf_rail_shapes = shape_lengths.loc[canonical_idx, ["route_id", "shape_id", "mode", "length_m"]].merge(
    gdf_shapes_utm[["shape_id", "geometry"]], on="shape_id",
)
gdf_rail_shapes = gpd.GeoDataFrame(gdf_rail_shapes, geometry="geometry", crs=CRS_UTM)
```

## Part A — Origin Processing (Network Nodes)

### A1 — Functional Type Flags

`nodes_on(gdf_nodes, gdf_links, ft_codes)` returns True for any node whose
N appears as endpoint A or B of at least one link whose FT code is in `ft_codes`.

Flags are **non-exclusive** — a node touching both a freeway and a ramp link
will be True for both `Freeway` and `Ramp`. Mutual exclusion is enforced later
in the topology cascade (§A3).

::: {#1c950572 .cell execution_count=12}
``` {.python .cell-code}
# ── Three mutually exclusive TDM link classes (2027 network year) ─────────
#
# FT_2027 code reference
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Class 1 — Freeway Mainline (FW_CODES):
#   12-15  Expressway (limited-access, divided)
#   22-26  MM freeway (posted 55-75 mph, MM series)
#   32-36  Freeway    (posted 55-75 mph, Fwy series)
#   40     Express / managed-access freeway
#   FT=2 AND DIRECTION=1: directional Principal Arterial links representing
#         physically separated roadways (e.g. divided expressways coded as PA).
#
# Class 2 — Ramps and CDs (RAMP_CODES):
#   20/30  Loop ramps  |  28/29  MM on/off ramps  |  41/42  Fwy on/off ramps
#   21/31  CD roads (collector-distributor geometry)
#
# Class 3 — Surface Streets (SURFACE_CODES):
#   2/3  Principal/Minor Arterial  |  4/5  Major/Minor Collector  |  6/7  Local/Unpaved
#   FT=2 links with DIRECTION=1 are excluded (they belong to Class 1 above).
#
# Filtered out at load time (not present in gdf_links):
#   1  Centroid connector (zone-to-network tap, not a physical road)
#   37 HOV lane  |  38 Managed lane  |  39 Managed-lane access point
#   Removed before any processing so they cannot inflate LinkCount/NeighborCount,
#   corrupt the pseudonode LinkClassCount check, pollute the direction cascade,
#   or produce spurious surface-type node classifications.
#
# Loaded but excluded from the three road classes:
#   70/80 Fixed transit  |  N ranges 10000-19999 and 50000-59999 (station nodes)
#   Transit geometry is handled separately in the FixedTransit snapping pass.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

FT_COL = "FT_2027"

# DIRECTION=1 flag: handles both numeric 1 and string "1" encodings
_oneway = gdf_links["ONEWAY"].astype(str).str.strip() == "1"

# Mutually exclusive link masks (LN_2027 > 0 already filtered at load time)

# 1. Freeway includes interstates and expressways/principal arterials that have directional travel
FWY_LINK_MASK = gdf_links[FT_COL].isin({22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 40}) | (
    gdf_links[FT_COL].isin({2, 12, 13, 14, 15}) & _oneway
)

# 2. Ramp and Collector-Distributor Roads share the same mask
RAMP_LINK_MASK = gdf_links[FT_COL].isin({20, 21, 28, 29, 30, 31, 41, 42})

# 3. Centroid Connectors (FT = 1)
CC_LINK_MASK = gdf_links[FT_COL] == 1

# 4. HOV and Managed Lanes (FT = 37, 38, 39)
MANAGED_LINK_MASK = gdf_links[FT_COL].isin({37, 38, 39})

# 5. Fixed Transit (FT = 70, 80) — loaded (at LN_2027==0) for Stage 3's
# connectivity graph, but excluded from all three road classes; transit
# geometry is handled separately in the FixedTransit snapping pass below.
TRANSIT_LINK_MASK = gdf_links[FT_COL].isin({70, 80})

# 6. Remaining Links get assigned as Surface Links
SURFACE_LINK_MASK = ~(
    FWY_LINK_MASK | RAMP_LINK_MASK | CC_LINK_MASK | MANAGED_LINK_MASK | TRANSIT_LINK_MASK
)

# FW_CODES: FT codes used for the freeway-priority direction cascade.
# FT=2+DIRECTION=1 is classified as freeway but excluded here because its
# DIRECTION value is a one-way flag, not a cardinal (NB/SB/EB/WB).
# Direction matching for those links is deferred to the geometric heading
# approach planned for the ramp refactor (Request 3).
FW_CODES = {12, 13, 14, 15, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 40}

gdf_nodes["Freeway"] = nodes_on(gdf_nodes, gdf_links[FWY_LINK_MASK])
gdf_nodes["Ramp"] = nodes_on(gdf_nodes, gdf_links[RAMP_LINK_MASK])
gdf_nodes["Surface"] = nodes_on(gdf_nodes, gdf_links[SURFACE_LINK_MASK])
gdf_nodes["FixedTransit"] = (
    nodes_on(gdf_nodes, gdf_links, {70, 80})
    | gdf_nodes["N"].between(10_000, 19_999)  # TRAX station nodes
    | gdf_nodes["N"].between(50_000, 59_999)  # FrontRunner station nodes
)

flag_cols = ["Freeway", "Ramp", "Surface", "FixedTransit"]
print("Flag counts:")
print(gdf_nodes[flag_cols].sum().rename("NodeCount").to_frame().to_string())
print(
    f"\nLinks by class — Freeway: {FWY_LINK_MASK.sum():,}  "
    f"| Ramp: {RAMP_LINK_MASK.sum():,}  "
    f"| Surface: {SURFACE_LINK_MASK.sum():,}"
)
```

### A2 — Link Count, Neighbor Count, and Direction

`count_links` adds `LinkCount` — raw endpoint references per node, used for the
distribution chart and diagnostics.

`count_neighbors` adds `NeighborCount` — the number of **distinct** neighboring
nodes. This is the topologically correct pseudonode test: `LinkCount` breaks on
bidirectional roads stored as two directional records (a pseudonode appears 4
times → LinkCount=4, not 2), while NeighborCount is always 2 for a true shape
vertex regardless of storage convention.

A node is an `is_pseudo` shape vertex if and only if all three conditions hold:
1. **NeighborCount == 2** — lies on a single path between two real junctions.
2. **LinkFTCount == 1** — all connected links share the same exact FT code.
   A node where FT changes (e.g. FT 32→33) has a real physical endpoint in the
   centerline data and must be sent to snapping.
3. **LinkLNCount == 1** — all connected links carry the same lane count.
   A lane-drop or lane-add node must not be dissolved away, as doing so would
   erase a model attribute boundary that affects TDM impedance.

`assign_node_directions` produces two direction columns (see docstring):
- `link_directions` — freeway-priority cascade; used in passes (a) and (c).
- `fw_directions`   — freeway links only, majority-vote; used in pass (b) gore nodes.

::: {#ea1196cf .cell execution_count=13}
``` {.python .cell-code}
gdf_nodes = count_links(gdf_nodes, gdf_links)
gdf_nodes = count_neighbors(gdf_nodes, gdf_links)
gdf_nodes = assign_node_directions(gdf_nodes, gdf_links, freeway_ft_codes=FW_CODES)

# Assign one class label per link using the already-defined mutually exclusive masks.
_link_class = pd.Series("other", index=gdf_links.index)
_link_class[FWY_LINK_MASK]  = "freeway"
_link_class[RAMP_LINK_MASK] = "ramp"
_link_class[SURFACE_LINK_MASK] = "surface"
_link_class[gdf_links[FT_COL].isin({70, 80})] = "transit"

# For each node, count how many distinct link classes touch it.
_stacked_class = pd.concat([
    gdf_links[["A"]].assign(cls=_link_class.values).rename(columns={"A": "N"}),
    gdf_links[["B"]].assign(cls=_link_class.values).rename(columns={"B": "N"}),
], ignore_index=True)
_class_counts = _stacked_class.groupby("N")["cls"].nunique()
gdf_nodes["LinkClassCount"] = gdf_nodes["N"].map(_class_counts).fillna(0).astype(int)

# Count distinct FT codes per node.
# Stricter than LinkClassCount: nodes where FT changes (e.g. FT=32→33) register
# LinkFTCount=2 even though both belong to the freeway class.  Used in the
# link true-shape dissolution step to preserve model link boundaries where posted
# speed or facility sub-type changes — dissolving those nodes would corrupt TDM impedance.
_stacked_ft = pd.concat([
    gdf_links[["A", FT_COL]].rename(columns={"A": "N"}),
    gdf_links[["B", FT_COL]].rename(columns={"B": "N"}),
], ignore_index=True)
_ft_counts = _stacked_ft.groupby("N")[FT_COL].nunique()
gdf_nodes["LinkFTCount"] = gdf_nodes["N"].map(_ft_counts).fillna(0).astype(int)

# Count distinct lane counts per node — lane-drop/lane-add nodes must be snapped
# even when FT is uniform, because dissolving them would erase the lane change.
_stacked_ln = pd.concat([
    gdf_links[["A", "LN_2027"]].rename(columns={"A": "N"}),
    gdf_links[["B", "LN_2027"]].rename(columns={"B": "N"}),
], ignore_index=True)
_ln_counts = _stacked_ln.groupby("N")["LN_2027"].nunique()
gdf_nodes["LinkLNCount"] = gdf_nodes["N"].map(_ln_counts).fillna(0).astype(int)

# Pseudonode: shape vertex on a single homogeneous path — no physical snap target.
# Requires uniform FT AND uniform lane count: a lane-drop node has a real physical
# endpoint in the centerline data and must not be dissolved away. is_pseudo gates
# Part A3's node_type assignment below (a pseudonode gets no node_type / is never
# sent to spatial snapping) and must stay this strict — a snapping target still
# needs FT/LN uniformity to be a safe physical match.
gdf_nodes["is_pseudo"] = (
    (gdf_nodes["NeighborCount"] == 2)
    & (gdf_nodes["LinkFTCount"] == 1)
    & (gdf_nodes["LinkLNCount"] == 1)
)

# Broader topological pass-through flag, for Stage 3 chain dissolution only
# (03_transfer_attributes.qmd) — NOT used for snapping eligibility here.
# NeighborCount==2 alone is a sufficient safety guarantee on its own: a node
# with exactly two distinct neighbors has exactly one way to walk through it,
# regardless of whether FT, lane count, or link class (freeway/ramp/surface
# designation) changes there. Dropping the uniform-FT/uniform-LN/uniform-class
# requirements here (unlike is_pseudo above) lets Stage 3 dissolve through
# real FT/lane-transition and class-transition nodes that have no physical
# vertex of their own — the dominant cause of `endpoints_only` pieces, see
# _plan/freeway-endpoint-pool-diagnosis.md and the node-30208 (Antelope Island
# Causeway) example that first surfaced it. A node with 3+ neighbors is never
# included regardless — with a real branch, topology alone can't tell you
# which branch continues the same physical road (see dissolve_pseudonodes'
# docstring), so it must stay a hard boundary.
gdf_nodes["is_topo_passthrough"] = gdf_nodes["NeighborCount"] == 2

print(f"Pseudonodes (NeighborCount==2, uniform FT+LN): {gdf_nodes['is_pseudo'].sum():,}")
print(f"  of which LinkCount==2: {(gdf_nodes['is_pseudo'] & (gdf_nodes['LinkCount'] == 2)).sum():,}")
print(f"  of which LinkCount> 2: {(gdf_nodes['is_pseudo'] & (gdf_nodes['LinkCount'] > 2)).sum():,}  ← bidirectional road pseudonodes")
print(f"Class-transition nodes (NeighborCount==2, multi-class): {((gdf_nodes['NeighborCount'] == 2) & (gdf_nodes['LinkClassCount'] > 1)).sum():,}  ← real junctions, must be snapped")
print(f"FT-transition nodes sent to snapping (NeighborCount==2, same class, diff FT): {((gdf_nodes['NeighborCount'] == 2) & (gdf_nodes['LinkClassCount'] == 1) & (gdf_nodes['LinkFTCount'] > 1)).sum():,}")
print(f"LN-transition nodes sent to snapping (NeighborCount==2, uniform FT, diff LN): {((gdf_nodes['NeighborCount'] == 2) & (gdf_nodes['LinkFTCount'] == 1) & (gdf_nodes['LinkLNCount'] > 1)).sum():,}")
print(f"is_topo_passthrough (NeighborCount==2, any FT/LN/class): {gdf_nodes['is_topo_passthrough'].sum():,}  ← Stage 3 dissolve set (broader than is_pseudo by {gdf_nodes['is_topo_passthrough'].sum() - gdf_nodes['is_pseudo'].sum():,})")
```

### A3 — Node Topology Classification

Eight mutually-exclusive `node_type` labels. Transit is evaluated first and
takes priority over all road-class combinations. The remaining seven labels
derive from the full combinatorics of the (Freeway, Ramp, Surface) flags.

HOV/managed-lane nodes (FT 37-39) were filtered at load time, so they
contribute no flags; those nodes fall to "surface" and are not snapped.
Pseudonodes (LinkCount == 2) are shape vertices with no physical counterpart.

::: {#c242580c .cell execution_count=15}
``` {.python .cell-code}
no_pseudo = ~gdf_nodes["is_pseudo"]

is_fwy_node     = gdf_nodes["Freeway"]      & no_pseudo
is_ramp_node    = gdf_nodes["Ramp"]         & no_pseudo
is_surface_node = gdf_nodes["Surface"]      & no_pseudo
# No no_pseudo gate here: is_pseudo means "uniform FT/LN across neighbors",
# a road-specific physical-endpoint test. A rail station is identified by
# GTFS proximity in D3, not by topology, so a station sitting on an
# otherwise-uniform two-neighbor stretch of track must still be a transit
# candidate — gating on no_pseudo would silently shrink D3's candidate pool.
is_transit_node = gdf_nodes["FixedTransit"]

# Full combinatorics of the three link classes → 7 node types.
# Transit is evaluated first — station nodes get "transit" regardless of any
# road-class links they may also touch.
# Most-specific road combinations (all three flags) are evaluated next.
gdf_nodes["node_type"] = np.select(
    [
        is_transit_node,                                  # fixed rail station
        is_fwy_node &  is_ramp_node &  is_surface_node,  # fwy+ramp+sf → at-grade interchange
        is_fwy_node &  is_ramp_node & ~is_surface_node,  # fwy+ramp    → elevated gore
        is_fwy_node & ~is_ramp_node &  is_surface_node,  # fwy+sf      → at-grade fwy crossing
        is_fwy_node & ~is_ramp_node & ~is_surface_node,  # fwy only    → pure mainline
        ~is_fwy_node & is_ramp_node &  is_surface_node,  # ramp+sf     → ramp terminal
        ~is_fwy_node & is_ramp_node & ~is_surface_node,  # ramp only   → mid-ramp
    ],
    ["transit", "gore_sf", "gore", "fwy_sf", "fwy", "ramp_sf", "ramp"],
    default="surface",
)

print("Node type distribution:")
print(gdf_nodes["node_type"].value_counts().rename("count").to_frame().to_string())
```

The endpoint layer makes topology and direction assignments explicit and

### B2 — Classify Segments

Three mutually exclusive boolean flags per segment. Primary authority is
`DOT_FCLASS` for freeway identification; `DOT_RTNAME` (UDOT LRS) supplements with
explicit route numbers and ramp/CD facility characters. `ONEWAY` in (`1`, `2`)
elevates divided Principal Arterials into the freeway class (domain CVDomain_OneWay:
0=Two-way, 1=One-way direction of arc, 2=One-way opposite direction of arc).

```
DOT_RTNAME layout (11 characters, zero-padded):
  [0:4]  Route number      e.g. "0015" = I-15, "0154" = Bangerter
  [4]    LRS direction     "P" = primary (NB/EB),  "N" = negative (SB/WB)
  [5]    Facility type     " " = mainline, "R" = ramp, "C" = collector-distributor
  [6:]   Sequence/suffix   varies
```

These flags flow into every endpoint pool and type-tier decision, making this
the **primary place to audit** when snapping results look wrong.

::: {#db61a33a .cell execution_count=19}
``` {.python .cell-code}
# ── Controlled-access corridors in the Wasatch Front study area ───────────
# Adding / removing a route here is the primary tuning lever for freeway coverage.
# These are the 4-character UDOT route numbers (DOT_RTNAME[0:4]).
FREEWAY_ROUTES = {
    "0015",   # Interstate 15         (primary N-S spine)
    "0067",   # Legacy Parkway        (limited-access, no ramps)
    "0080",   # Interstate 80         (E-W, SLC to Parley's Canyon)
    "0084",   # Interstate 84         (Ogden corridor)
    "0089",   # US-89                 (surface in places — watch for mis-classification)
    "0092",   # Timpanogos Highway    (SR-92, American Fork Canyon)
    "0154",   # Bangerter Highway     (semi-controlled ring road)
    "0177",   # West Davis Corridor   (new build, limited segments)
    "0201",   # SR-201                (West Valley connector)
    "0215",   # Interstate 215        (belt route, SLC)
}

rtname  = active_cl["DOT_RTNAME"].fillna("")

# ── Shared exclusion flags ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Ramp/CD character check: DOT_RTNAME LIKE '%R%' or '%C%', excluding DupRoute.
_has_R_or_C = rtname.str.contains("R", na=False) | rtname.str.contains("C", na=False)
_not_duprt  = rtname != "DupRoute"
_not_ramp_cd = ~_has_R_or_C | ~_not_duprt  # True when segment is NOT a ramp/CD

# ── Class 1: Freeway Mainline ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Primary: DOT_FCLASS identifies interstate / other freeway geometry.
# Secondary: explicit UDOT route number is a controlled-access corridor.
# Tertiary: Principal Arterial with ONEWAY in ('1','2') represents a
#           physically separated directional roadway.
#           ONEWAY domain (CVDomain_OneWay): 0=Two-way, 1=One-way direction
#           of arc, 2=One-way opposite direction of arc.
# All three require exclusion of ramp/CD facility chars and DupRoute aliases.
_is_fclass_fwy = active_cl["DOT_FCLASS"].isin(["Interstate", "Other Freeway"])
_is_named_fwy  = rtname.str.slice(0, 4).isin(FREEWAY_ROUTES)
_is_dir_pa = (
    (active_cl["DOT_FCLASS"] == "Principal Arterial")
    & active_cl["ONEWAY"].isin(["1", "2"])
)

active_cl["is_freeway"] = (
    (_is_fclass_fwy | _is_named_fwy | _is_dir_pa)
    & ~_has_R_or_C
    & _not_duprt
)

# ── Class 2: Ramps and CDs ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Strictly determined by DOT_RTNAME structure: any R or C facility character,
# excluding the DupRoute administrative alias.
active_cl["is_interchange"] = _has_R_or_C & _not_duprt

# ── Class 3: Surface Streets ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Everything that is not freeway mainline or ramp/CD.
# Explicitly excludes DOT_FCLASS values that fall outside the three classes
# (already filtered in B1, but guard here for completeness).
active_cl["is_surface"] = (
    ~active_cl["is_freeway"]
    & ~active_cl["is_interchange"]
    & active_cl["DOT_FCLASS"].notna()
    & ~active_cl["DOT_FCLASS"].isin(["Interstate", "Other Freeway", "Instituitional", ""])  # note: source-data typo
)

print("Segment-level classification:")
print(f"  is_freeway     (mainline):   {active_cl['is_freeway'].sum():,}")
print(f"  is_interchange (ramp / CD):  {active_cl['is_interchange'].sum():,}")
print(f"  is_surface     (all others): {active_cl['is_surface'].sum():,}")
print(f"  unclassified   (none):       {(~active_cl['is_freeway'] & ~active_cl['is_interchange'] & ~active_cl['is_surface']).sum():,}")
print(f"  both fwy + ic  (gore segs):  {(active_cl['is_freeway'] & active_cl['is_interchange']).sum():,}")
print(f"  total active:                {len(active_cl):,}")
```

### B4 — Deduplicate by Tolerance-Based Clustering

Cluster raw endpoints by true single-linkage distance (`cluster_endpoints`,
`ENDPOINT_CLUSTER_TOLERANCE_M` = 1cm) rather than a rounded-coordinate grid
bucket — two points 2mm apart that happen to round into different 1cm grid
cells (e.g. `10.004999` → `10.00` vs `10.005001` → `10.01`) are now correctly
merged. Aggregate type flags with OR — a cluster is `is_freeway=True` if any
freeway segment terminates there. The output geometry keeps the exact
(unrounded) coordinate of one contributing raw endpoint rather than
reconstructing a point from the rounded key, so `gdf_ep_unique` — and every
node later snapped onto it — stays bit-exact with a real `CandidateTDMRoadLinks`
vertex instead of sitting on a 1cm quantization grid. `x_round`/`y_round` are
still carried through (first raw point) for QGIS inspection and for
`link_utils.resolve_snap_coords`'s downstream nearest-vertex lookup, which
is out of scope for this change.

::: {#58aa660a .cell execution_count=21}
``` {.python .cell-code}
gdf_ep_raw["cluster_id"] = cluster_endpoints(
    gdf_ep_raw, tolerance_m=ENDPOINT_CLUSTER_TOLERANCE_M
)

cluster_sizes = gdf_ep_raw.groupby("cluster_id").size()
print(
    f"Endpoint clusters: {len(cluster_sizes):,} clusters "
    f"from {len(gdf_ep_raw):,} raw points (tolerance={ENDPOINT_CLUSTER_TOLERANCE_M}m)"
)
print(f"Cluster size distribution: {cluster_sizes.value_counts().sort_index().to_dict()}")

# Chaining-risk QA: single-linkage clustering can in principle chain several
# close-but-distinct vertices together. Flag any cluster whose raw points
# span more than 2x tolerance end-to-end (bounding-box diagonal as a cheap
# upper bound on max pairwise distance).
_span = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "cluster_id": gdf_ep_raw["cluster_id"],
        "x": gdf_ep_raw.geometry.x.values,
        "y": gdf_ep_raw.geometry.y.values,
    }
).groupby("cluster_id").agg(x_span=("x", np.ptp), y_span=("y", np.ptp))
_span["diag_m"] = np.hypot(_span["x_span"], _span["y_span"])
_chaining_risk = _span[_span["diag_m"] > 2 * ENDPOINT_CLUSTER_TOLERANCE_M]
if len(_chaining_risk):
    print(f"WARNING: {len(_chaining_risk)} cluster(s) span > {2 * ENDPOINT_CLUSTER_TOLERANCE_M:.2f}m — possible chaining:")
    print(_chaining_risk.sort_values("diag_m", ascending=False).head(10).to_string())
else:
    print("No chaining risk detected — all clusters within 2x tolerance.")

ep_agg = gdf_ep_raw.groupby("cluster_id", as_index=False).agg(
    x_round=("x_round", "first"),
    y_round=("y_round", "first"),
    is_freeway=("is_freeway", "any"),
    is_interchange=("is_interchange", "any"),
    is_surface=("is_surface", "any"),
    fw_route_count=(
        "dot_rtname",
        lambda s: s[gdf_ep_raw.loc[s.index, "is_freeway"]].str[:4].nunique(),

    geometry=("geometry", "first"),

gdf_ep_unique = gpd.GeoDataFrame(ep_agg, geometry="geometry", crs=CRS_UTM)
gdf_ep_unique["ep_uid"] = gdf_ep_unique["cluster_id"]
```

## Part C — Interchange Node Direction Enrichment

For interchange-only nodes (pass c), the directional signal is inherited one hop

``` {.python .cell-code}
# Build a flat edge list: (node_N, FT, DIRECTION) — vectorised via pd.concat
edges = pd.concat([
    gdf_links[["A", "FT_2027", "DIRECTION"]].rename(columns={"A": "N"}),
    gdf_links[["B", "FT_2027", "DIRECTION"]].rename(columns={"B": "N"}),
], ignore_index=True)
edges["is_freeway_link"] = edges["FT_2027"].isin(FW_CODES)
edges["DIRECTION"]       = edges["DIRECTION"].astype(str).str.strip().str.upper()

CARDINAL = {"NB", "SB", "EB", "WB"}
```

export so at-grade crossing snaps can be verified before running surface snapping.

``` {.python .cell-code}
# ── Endpoint pools ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Each pool is now built from node_utils.allowed_ep_types(), which reads
# straight off _TYPE_TIER — the same table _spatial_snap uses to score
# candidates — instead of a hand-typed ep_type list. Diagnosis (2026-07-16)
# found the previous hand-typed pools had silently drifted narrower than
# _TYPE_TIER (and this section's own comments) already declared permitted:
# e.g. ("fwy", "gore"): 1 was documented as a Tier-1 fallback, but "gore"
# endpoints were never actually in the fwy pool below, so that fallback was
# dead code. Freeway/interchange node types took the brunt of it: their
# nearest real physical vertex is disproportionately a Tier-1 type one class
# over (arcpy only cuts centerlines at interchanges, not at the FT/lane
# -transition points that generate many freeway model nodes), and that
# vertex was almost always well within the search radius — median 100-150m
# vs. a 500m threshold — it just never reached the candidate pool. See
# node_utils.allowed_ep_types docstring for the full writeup. Any deviation
# from the raw tier table below is a deliberate, separately-justified
# business rule, called out inline.

# Pass (a) — fwy nodes → {fwy, gore, fwy_sf} (_TYPE_TIER tier ≤ 1 for "fwy").
#   ramp/surface are absent from _TYPE_TIER's "fwy" row entirely (not merely
#   tier>1), so they stay excluded — the divided-highway-collapse protection
#   this pool was designed for is unchanged, only the gore/fwy_sf Tier-1
#   fallback (previously dead) is now reachable.
ep_fwy_only = gdf_ep_unique[gdf_ep_unique["ep_type"].isin(allowed_ep_types("fwy"))].copy()

# Pass (a2) — fwy_sf nodes → _TYPE_TIER gives {fwy_sf, fwy, surface, gore};
#   surface is deliberately dropped here — if no fwy-class endpoint is within
#   range the node falls through to D2 (surface pass) where surface endpoints
#   are available under D2's own (more appropriate) direction logic.
ep_fwy_sf = gdf_ep_unique[
    gdf_ep_unique["ep_type"].isin(allowed_ep_types("fwy_sf") - {"surface"})
].copy()

# Pass (b) — gore + gore_sf nodes share one pool: the union of each node
#   type's _TYPE_TIER-allowed set is {fwy, fwy_sf, gore, ramp, ramp_sf}.
#   "fwy" is further restricted to multi-route hub interchanges
#   (fw_route_count >= 2) — a deliberate heuristic beyond what _TYPE_TIER
#   encodes, kept to avoid over-matching a gore node to an isolated
#   single-route fwy endpoint that merely happens to be nearby.
_gore_allowed = allowed_ep_types("gore") | allowed_ep_types("gore_sf")
ep_gore = gdf_ep_unique[
    gdf_ep_unique["ep_type"].isin(_gore_allowed)
    & ~((gdf_ep_unique["ep_type"] == "fwy") & (gdf_ep_unique["fw_route_count"] < 2))
].copy()

# Pass (c) — ramp nodes → _TYPE_TIER gives {ramp, gore, ramp_sf}.
ep_ic_only = gdf_ep_unique[gdf_ep_unique["ep_type"].isin(allowed_ep_types("ramp"))].copy()

print(f"Pass (a)  pool — fwy, gore, fwy_sf:                 {len(ep_fwy_only):,}")
print(f"Pass (a2) pool — fwy_sf, fwy, gore:                 {len(ep_fwy_sf):,}")
print(f"Pass (b)  pool — gore, fwy(hub), ramp, fwy_sf, ramp_sf: {len(ep_gore):,}")
print(f"Pass (c)  pool — ramp, gore, ramp_sf:               {len(ep_ic_only):,}")

# ── Node masks ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# gore_sf (fwy+ramp+surface): included in pass (b) alongside gore nodes;
#   _TYPE_TIER gives it access to fwy_sf/ramp_sf/fwy/ramp endpoints at Tier-1
```

### D3 — Transit Snapping

FixedTransit nodes snap to Light Rail (TRAX) and Commuter Rail (FrontRunner)
physical track, not raw GTFS stop points. Bus stops are excluded. Twin
platforms are merged to a station centroid, then that centroid is projected
onto the nearest point of its own mode's dissolved shape (perpendicular
projection, not nearest vertex or stop point) using the same
`snap_cc_nodes` nearest-line engine already used for CC/external attachment
nodes — GTFS stop coordinates are still several to tens of metres offset
from the actual track alignment, and this removes that offset before the
model node ever snaps to anything.

::: {#a6c734ed .cell execution_count=36}

``` {.python .cell-code}
# physically distinct platforms — merging across modes there would produce a

# geometry column is plain shapely objects after the lambda — no inherited CRS.
```

## Debug Export

Unified debug package covering all snapping passes. Every layer carries `snap_rule`
and `node_type` so QGIS can filter by pass (e.g. show only `Freeway_Only`) or by
topology class (e.g. show only `ramp_sf` ramp terminals) — or display everything at
once. The `endpoint_layer` was already written in step B7.

`node_type` to topology mapping for QGIS filters:

| `node_type` | Topology |
|---|---|
| `transit` | Fixed rail station (TRAX / FrontRunner) |
| `fwy` | Freeway mainline only |
| `gore` | Freeway + ramp (elevated) |
| `gore_sf` | Freeway + ramp + surface (at-grade) |
| `fwy_sf` | Freeway + surface (at-grade crossing) |
| `ramp` | Ramp only (mid-ramp) |
| `ramp_sf` | Ramp + surface (ramp terminal) |
| `surface` | Surface street only |

### CC Attachment Nodes

Centroid connector attachment nodes are the network-side endpoints of FT_2027 = 1
(centroid connector) links — the taps where zone centroids connect to the road
network. Zone centroids themselves (N < 3600) are excluded; only the network
attachment nodes (N ≥ 3600) are retained.

These nodes are snapped to the nearest **point** on the nearest physical
centerline (perpendicular projection, not nearest vertex or endpoint) using a
simple STRtree lookup — no direction filtering, no greedy assignment.
Centroid connectors essentially never attach to freeway mainline (checked
directly: 23 of several thousand real-road links touching a CC attachment
node are FT 31/33/35, the mainline codes), so the undirected divided-highway
collision risk that rules out this approach for road-node snapping doesn't
apply here. The result is written as a second layer in `nodes_snapped.gpkg`.

A CC attachment node sometimes already coincides with a real junction that
the direction-aware greedy snapper above already placed — `already_snapped`
flags those directly against this notebook's own `gdf_nodes_snapped` output
(the `snapped` column), not inferred from anything else. `use_as_split =
snap_resolved & ~already_snapped` is the one column Stage 2/3 actually
consume: reusing an already-snapped node's independently-computed nearest-
point coordinate here would plant a second, slightly different split a few
cm away from the real one, producing a sliver instead of a clean cut.
Unresolved nodes (> 100 m) are simply excluded — same as any other unsnapped
node, no special handling.

### External Station Nodes

External station nodes (`EXTERNAL_ = 1` on the node table, N 3601–3629) are
gateway points where the model network intentionally truncates at the edge
of the modelled region — canyon passes, state lines (e.g. "I-15 to
Tremonton", "SR 190 Guardsman Pass"). Like CC attachment nodes, they get the
same nearest-point-on-line treatment (not nearest-vertex) and the same
`already_snapped`/`use_as_split` columns, and are written as a third
`nodes_snapped.gpkg` layer.

The same 100 m cutoff as CC nodes is kept deliberately tight: several
external nodes sit 1–13 km from any WF-county centerline (true remote
boundary points where our centerline extract simply doesn't reach), and
snapping those to whatever point happens to be nearest would be a misleading
match rather than a real one — better left unresolved (excluded, same as any

### Re-flagging Mid-Link Attachment Nodes as Hard Boundaries

`NeighborCount` (Part A, top of this notebook) is computed from the
FT_2027-filtered link table, so a CC node's FT=1 spur is invisible to it. When
the model inserts a CC/external attachment node strictly between two
intersections — coding the through road as two separate link rows,
`intersection1 → node` and `node → intersection2` — that node sees only its
two real-road neighbors and looks like an ordinary shape point:
`is_topo_passthrough = True`. `03_transfer_attributes.qmd`'s pass-through
dissolve then silently walks through it, merging both halves into one chain
with no split at the node's true location and no separate attribute transfer
for either half. `use_as_split` (computed above) is exactly the set of nodes
where this applies: resolved, and not already snapped/handled elsewhere. A
node already at a real junction already has `is_topo_passthrough = False` and
needs no change.

Rail station nodes just snapped in D3 have the exact same failure mode —
a mid-line station (e.g. an intermediate TRAX stop with no other junction)
sees only its two rail neighbors and looks like an ordinary pass-through
point, but it's now a genuine split point for the rail pieces built in
`02_create_link.qmd`'s Part F — so it's folded into the same patch below.

CC/external connectors that land *on the rail lines themselves* (not
stations — WFRC's MasterNet wires a number of TAZ centroid connectors
directly onto an ordinary mid-corridor rail node, e.g. representing walk/
park-and-ride access to a nearby line), and genuine multi-neighbor rail
junctions (wyes, crossovers, double-track switches — see below), are the
two cases excluded from this patch. A curb-cut on a surface street is a
genuine physical interruption — both halves legitimately get their own
attribution and vertex. A rail corridor has no equivalent interruption: a
centroid connector is a zonal-access edge, not a boarding point, and a
track junction with no real GTFS station on it is not a passenger-facing
split either, so the physical track runs straight through uninterrupted in
both cases (`02_create_link.qmd`'s Part F never cuts the canonical GTFS
shape there, only at real stations). Patching these nodes to hard
boundaries anyway forces a split in the *model* chain at a point the
*physical* piece was never split — the piece's real endpoints (two actual
stations) can then never coordinate-match any dissolved chain, showing up
as `endpoints_only`/`a_only`/`b_only` on every affected route segment.

`LinkFTCount == 1 & LinkLNCount == 1` restricted to `FixedTransit` nodes
(Part A2's uniformity check, computed for every node regardless of
neighbor count) safely identifies "every connected link is the same rail
mode at the same lane count" — a node bridging rail with a different link
class, or two different rail FT codes (e.g. where light rail and commuter
rail interline), fails this check and is correctly left as a hard
boundary. Unlike `is_pseudo`, this doesn't also require `NeighborCount ==
2`, so it additionally catches genuine 3+-neighbor rail junctions (a wye,
a double-track crossover, a turnback) where the model network forks but
the canonical GTFS shape doesn't — those still need `is_topo_passthrough`
force-set to `True` (not just excluded from the hard-boundary patch below)
since a real junction never starts out `NeighborCount == 2`.
`dissolve_pseudonodes` (`_src/link_utils.py`) resolves the resulting
multi-way ambiguity geometrically: at any pass-through node with more than
one forward continuation, it picks the straightest one (smallest turn
angle from the incoming bearing) — validated against all 50 such rail
junctions network-wide, only 7 of which even have a second-best option
within 40° of the best, i.e. this is never a close call.

::: {#cad763fc .cell execution_count=50}
